before.title: Coolant Loss from Water Pump / Thermostat Housing
before.description: TSI Kodiaqs (1.4 and 2.0 TSI) can develop coolant leaks from the plastic water-pump/thermostat housing assembly, a recurring VAG-engine weakness. Owners report a slowly dropping coolant level that dealers sometimes struggle to pinpoint, and in some cases a replaced pump leaks again, indicating it is not fully resolved. If ignored, coolant loss risks overheating.
before.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system to locate the leak, replace the integrated water pump/thermostat housing (often combined with the thermostat and seals), and properly bleed the system to remove trapped air.

before.title: DPF Clogging and AdBlue/SCR System Faults on 2.0 TDI Diesels
before.description: Diesel Kodiaqs used mainly for short urban trips frequently suffer incomplete diesel particulate filter (DPF) regeneration, leading to a clogged filter and recurring warning lights. The associated SCR/AdBlue system (urea pump, injector, NOx sensors) is complex, and a single failed component triggers an emissions fault, sometimes with a no-restart countdown warning. Symptoms include power loss, black smoke, strong exhaust smell and a check-engine light.
before.solution: Perform a forced/active regeneration and drive at sustained highway speed (around 100 km / ~20-25 min at ~3,000 rpm) to clear the filter; clean or replace the DPF if saturated. AdBlue faults require diagnosing and replacing the specific failed component (NOx sensor, urea injector or pump) and topping up/correcting AdBlue.

before.title: DSG Dual-Clutch Transmission Jerking and Mechatronic Failure
before.description: The 6- and 7-speed DSG dual-clutch automatics fitted to many Kodiaqs (notably 2.0 TSI 190hp and 2.0 TDI 150hp) suffer jerky/hesitant low-speed shifting and, more seriously, failure of the mechatronic control unit. Owners report two failure waves: a software-related phase around 20,000-30,000 km and a mechanical-wear phase around 80,000-120,000 km. When the mechatronics fail, the gearbox can lose gears (e.g. only even gears or no reverse), enter limp/emergency mode, or delay 20-30 seconds engaging Drive followed by a clunk.
before.solution: Software/adaptation updates resolve early shudder cases. Mechanical failures require mechatronic unit replacement or full DSG overhaul, plus the recommended 40,000-mile DSG oil-and-filter service (not the 80k some quote) to prolong clutch pack and mechatronic life.
symptoms: Delayed engagement from Park to Drive
Loss of reverse or only even gears
Clunk or jolt when gear finally engages

before.title: 7-Speed DSG (DQ381) Low-Speed Hesitation and Jerking
before.description: Kodiaq with the DQ381 wet-clutch 7-speed DSG (replaced the earlier DQ500 around 2018) exhibits low-speed hesitation, jerking from a stop, and harsh 1→2 upshifts. Skoda has issued multiple software updates but the issue persists for many owners. Worsens with stop-start traffic.
before.solution: Apply latest DQ381 software update (often free under goodwill from main dealer). Mechatronic refurbishment in severe cases (€1,500-€2,500). Some specialists offer adaptation resets that improve symptoms temporarily.
symptoms: Occasional loss of drive during shifts

before.title: General Electrical Faults: Central Locking, Sensors and Climate Control
before.description: Electrical gremlins are the single most-reported complaint area on the Kodiaq across both petrol and diesel cars. Owners report central-locking malfunctions, faulty sensors, and intermittent climate-control failures (including weak air-conditioning cooling from defective compressors or refrigerant loss, often after 25,000-40,000 km). Most repairs are completed within a day and many fall under warranty, but a minority require extended workshop time.
before.solution: Diagnose with VAG-specific equipment to isolate the failed sensor, module or actuator; remedies range from software updates and reflashes to replacing the faulty sensor, locking actuator, or A/C compressor and recharging refrigerant.

before.title: Infotainment Screen Freezing, Blanking and Rebooting
before.description: The Bolero and Columbus infotainment head units commonly freeze, go blank, lose Bluetooth/connectivity, or spontaneously reboot while driving. The fault is most prevalent on early production (roughly 2016-2018) units and is a known VAG software issue. Climate and navigation functions tied to the touchscreen can also become unresponsive during an episode.
before.solution: Skoda issued multiple software/firmware updates that resolve many cases; a forced reboot (holding the power/volume button ~10-15 seconds) clears momentary freezes. Persistent failures require replacement of the infotainment unit under warranty or as a paid repair.

before.title: iV Plug-in Hybrid 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain
before.description: Kodiaq iV PHEV models suffer 12V auxiliary battery drain similar to VW Group ID series. Modules fail to enter deep sleep, draining the 12V battery in 5-10 days of inactivity. Vehicle then refuses to start (HV battery is fine but 12V is required for system boot).
before.solution: Software update from dealer addresses some causes. If 12V battery is damaged from repeated deep discharge, replacement required (€150-€250 AGM). For vehicles parked >1 week regularly, install trickle charger.
symptoms: Dashboard shows multiple warning lights when jumped

before.title: Recall: Takata Driver Airbag Inflator May Rupture
before.description: Early Kodiaqs (2016-2017 build) are part of the wider Takata recall: the airbag propellant can deteriorate over time, and on deployment excessive internal pressure may burst the inflator body, sending metal fragments into the cabin. A separate recall also covers driver airbags built Jan-Feb 2018 that could inflate too slowly in a crash.
before.solution: Free recall remedy — the affected airbag inflator/module is inspected and replaced by a Skoda dealer. Owners should check their VIN against Skoda's recall campaign portal.
